betterCitation: Anne Morrow Lindbergh, Gift from the Sea, chapter 2, Channelled Whelk (Pantheon, 1955)
reason: Refuted as the verifier would ship it, and the fault is in the hedge rather than in the quotation. I tried to do better than the verifier and could not. Archive.org holds twenty-three copies of Gift from the Sea, from giftfromsea00lind (1955) onward, and every full-text route into them failed from here: the search-inside endpoints returned nothing at all and the page-scrape service returned nothing, so no scan page could be opened. The Google Books API answered 429, quota exceeded, exactly as the verifier reported. So the book was not opened by me either, and wordingChecked is false on purpose. What I could add: two independent secondary readings agree on chapter 2. Wikiquote gives Gift from the Sea (1955), Ch. 2, and prints the sentence with its continuation, That is why so much of social life is exhausting; one is wearing a mask. A chapter by chapter reading of Channelled Whelk cites p. 26, inside a run of citations from p. 4 to p. 28, but it quotes the sentence with ellipses, as the most exhausting thing in life...being insincere, so it corroborates the placement and NOT the wording. Lindbergh's authorship is not in doubt and the sentence is not on the misattribution list; chapter 2 of the book is Channelled Whelk, so the chapter title is right. THE REFUTABLE THING is the source line the verifier built. It reads Attributed to Anne Morrow Lindbergh, which puts the hedge on the author when the author is the one part nobody disputes, and the verifier's own note says so: Lindbergh's authorship is not in doubt; the placement inside the book is what went unconfirmed. The card prints the source line as the byline and has no author field, so this would print a byline saying Attributed to Anne Morrow Lindbergh over a sentence that is hers beyond argument. That is a false signal in the direction the standard cares least about, and it breaks rule 5, which says the source line leads with the author's name. It is also off this track's own convention for a hedge: 04-fict-08 is a HEDGE and its source line leads with Sor Juana Inés de la Cruz plainly, with the whole hedge living in the note. The proposal as the curator wrote it also had no Attributed to; the verifier added it. The betterCitation above restores the plain byline and leaves the hedge where it belongs, in the note, which must say that the book was not opened, that the wording rests on reference sites rather than on any edition, and that chapter 2 is corroborated but the page is not. A SECOND, WEAKER ATTACK I will name and not press: Gift from the Sea is often shelved as inspirational writing, and the out of scope list bars self-help and motivational writing. I do not think that carries, since the book is a literary meditation of 1955 with a settled place in the essay canon and the tag Essay is right for its form. On the remaining checks it is clean: not scripture, film, lyric, proverb, business or oratory; pre-1999; publishable, with nothing needing a warning; a complete sentence ending in a full stop; no dash and no straight quote in the source line, which runs 100 characters as the verifier wrote it and 86 as corrected; shipped.js returns no hit, no near-hit, zero for the year, not banned, not at cap; no second Lindbergh in the month. The theme fits well, since it argues for sincerity from fatigue rather than from virtue.

residual: Ship as a HEDGE with the plain byline and the honest note, in the shape 04-fict-08 uses: name the author, then say in the note that the book was not opened, that chapter 2 Channelled Whelk is corroborated by two independent secondary readings and the reported p. 26 is not, and that the exact wording has not been seen in any edition. If the month can fill without it, a line whose wording no edition has confirmed is the first one to drop.
